findings.summary: The page says asyncio.to_thread fixes CPU-bound work, but it only helps with blocking I/O: the GIL still serialises pure-Python CPU work.
findings.evidence: "Blocking/CPU work: `await asyncio.to_thread(fn)` keeps the loop live"
findings.fix: Change it to "Blocking I/O: `await asyncio.to_thread(fn)`; CPU-bound: `loop.run_in_executor(ProcessPoolExecutor(), fn)`".

findings.summary: The worker loop tests for truthiness, so any falsy item (0, "", [], {}) stops the worker early, not just the None sentinel the note describes.
findings.evidence: "while (x := await q.get()):" with note "None sentinel ends the loop"
findings.fix: Use `while (x := await q.get()) is not None:`.
